homogeneous Gaussian spatial regression without nugget

definitions.name: quasi-uniform signed-cross-tail experiment class
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal M=\{(P_N,\mathcal S_N)_{N\ge1}: d\in\{1,2\},\ D\in\mathfrak D_{\mathrm{BL}}(d,D_0),\ c_mN^{-1/d}\le h_N\le C_mN^{-1/d},\ \delta_N\ge c_sh_N,\ \beta\in\operatorname{int}(\mathcal B),\ 1/2<p_{\min}\le p\le p_{\max}<1,\ A\in[-A_{\max},A_{\max}],\ (c_X,c_W,\alpha_X,\alpha_W,\alpha_C)\in\mathcal K_{\mathrm{nuis}},\ (X,W)\in\mathcal G_{\mathrm{stat}}(F;\mathbb R^d),\ F=(f_{k\ell})_{k,\ell\in\{X,W\}},\ f_Xf_W-f_{XW}^2\ge\rho f_Xf_W,\ (Y(s_{i,N}))_{i=1}^N=(\beta X(s_{i,N})+W(s_{i,N}))_{i=1}^N\}\).

definitions.name: three-scale exact affine stencil algorithm
definitions.construction: Partition the fixed cube \(D_0\) into macrocells of side \(S Lh_N\), assign balanced groups \(j\in\{0,1,2\}\), select observed sites nearest the center and axis targets at radius \(2^jLh_N\), and set \(w_{Nja}=w^0-F_{Nja}^{\mathsf T}(F_{Nja}F_{Nja}^{\mathsf T})^{-1}F_{Nja}w^0\).

definitions.name: studentized cone-profile confidence set
definitions.construction: Compute \(m_N\), \(q_N\), \(H_N\), and \(\widehat\gamma_N\); minimize analytically over the line loading for each \(p\in[p_{\min},p_{\max}]\); set \(T_N(b)=N\widehat\gamma_N^{-1}d_{H_N}(m_N-b\mathbf 1,\mathcal C_N)^2\), \(C_N=\{b\in\mathcal B:T_N(b)\le\chi^2_{2,1-\alpha}\}\), and \(\widehat\beta_N\in\operatorname*{arg\,min}_{b\in\mathcal B}T_N(b)\).

definitions.name: attainable Gaussian-tube calibration handle
definitions.construction: Analyze \(d_{H_N}(G_N+\lambda_N q_N(p),\mathcal C_N)^2\) by compactness of \((q_N,H_N)\), Gaussian tube probabilities for bounded \(\lambda_N\), separated tangent and endpoint half-plane limits for diverging \(|\lambda_N|\), and certified interval arithmetic over the physically attainable \((\lambda_N,p)\) set.

statements.statement: For fixed sufficiently large \(L\) and then fixed sufficiently large \(S\), the three-scale exact affine stencil algorithm produces three disjoint groups with \(|\mathcal G_{N,j}|\asymp N\), uniformly bounded weights and stencil degree, \(\sum_{\ell}w_{Nja\ell}=0\), and \(\sum_{\ell}w_{Nja\ell}s_{Nja\ell}=0\). Consequently, constant and quadratic analytic covariance terms cancel exactly, boundary loss is \(O(1)\) as a fraction of \(N\), and the normalized off-diagonal filtered marginal covariances are bounded by \(C(1+r/h_N)^{-3}\).
statements.justification: This is the design-uniform construction that removes the \(d=2\) first-difference bias and logarithmic variance obstruction.
statements.gap: Loh, Sun and Wen and Keshavarz, Nguyen and Scott use selected irregular designs or prescribed preconditioners; this lemma must work for every design in \(\mathcal M\).
statements.consumer: It supplies boundary-safe sparse filters for the joint experiment in Theorem 1.

statements.statement: There is a constant \(c_{\star}>0\) such that uniformly in the allowed designs and \(p,u\in[p_{\min},p_{\max}]\), \(\inf_{b,b'\in\mathbb R}\|a\mathbf 1+bq_N(p)-b'q_N(u)\|\ge c_{\star}|a|\) for every \(a\in\mathbb R\). The same bound holds on the diagonal \(u=p\) with the secant replaced by \(q_N'(p)\). For the ideal geometric curve \(q_N(p)=(1,t,t^2)^{\mathsf T}\), \(t=2^{2p-1}\), the normal vector \((tu,-t-u,1)^{\mathsf T}\) gives \((t-1)(u-1)\) against \(\mathbf 1\).
statements.justification: Uniform secant and tangent separation identifies the slope even when the tail amplitude is zero and \(p\) disappears.
statements.gap: Neither spectral-adjustment identification nor scalar quadratic variation contains this three-scale divided-difference modulus on perturbed designs.
statements.consumer: It turns moment-space Gaussian radius bounds into root-\(N\) confidence-set diameter and risk bounds.

statements.statement: Uniformly over \((P_N,\mathcal S_N)\in\mathcal M\), \(\sqrt N\{m_N-\beta\mathbf 1-B_Nq_N(p)\}\) is approximated by \(N_3(0,\gamma H_N)\) in bounded-Lipschitz distance, \(0<c\le\lambda_{\min}(H_N)\le\lambda_{\max}(H_N)\le C<\infty\), and \(\widehat\gamma_N/\gamma\to1\) in probability. The approximation is uniform for signed \(A_N\), including \(A_N=0\), local \(\sqrt N B_N\), diverging \(|\sqrt N B_N|\), and \(p_N\) approaching either fixed endpoint. The proof bounds the exact finite covariance matrices and explicitly makes the boundary, sampling alias, denominator-linearization, and Mat\'ern Bessel remainders \(o(N^{-1/2})\).
statements.justification: The uniform actual-design experiment is the statistical kernel absent from the existing identification and fixed-domain covariance literature.
statements.gap: Lim and Stein prove filtered lattice cross-periodogram normality, and Keshavarz et al. prove scalar irregular-lattice quadratic-form normality; neither result covers these ratio moments, arbitrary quasi-uniform geometry, or weak disappearance of \(p\).
statements.consumer: It converts Guan et al.'s local-scale identifying idea into feasible frequentist inference without nugget variation.

statements.statement: The studentized cone-profile confidence set \(C_N\) and estimator \(\widehat\beta_N\) satisfy \(\liminf_{N\to\infty}\inf_{(P_N,\mathcal S_N)\in\mathcal M}P_N\{\beta\in C_N\}\ge1-\alpha\), \(\sup_{(P_N,\mathcal S_N)\in\mathcal M}E_{P_N}[\operatorname{diam}(C_N)]\le C_{\alpha}N^{-1/2}\), and \(\sup_{(P_N,\mathcal S_N)\in\mathcal M}E_{P_N}[(\widehat\beta_N-\beta)^2]\le C N^{-1}\). These relations hold through every sequence \(A_N\to0\) without consistently estimating \(p\) or any Mat\'ern range.
statements.justification: It shows that adaptation across the singular face \(A=0\) costs neither consistency nor the parametric rate.
statements.gap: Datta and Stein establish consistent estimability and local-difference estimators but do not provide uniform coverage, expected diameter, or risk through a vanishing signed cross-tail.
statements.consumer: Conditional on the Gaussian Mat\'ern and quasi-uniform diagnostics, it provides an honest homogeneous-slope analysis for the county-centroid PM2.5 and COVID-19 setting of Burman, Ogburn and Datta.

statements.statement: For every \(0<\alpha<1/2\), there are constants \(c_{\alpha},c>0\) such that every sequence of confidence intervals \(I_N\) with \(\liminf_N\inf_{(P_N,\mathcal S_N)\in\mathcal M}P_N\{\beta\in I_N\}\ge1-\alpha\) obeys \(\liminf_N\sqrt N\sup_{(P_N,\mathcal S_N)\in\mathcal M}E_{P_N}[\operatorname{length}(I_N)]\ge c_{\alpha}\), and every estimator \(\widetilde\beta_N\) obeys \(\liminf_N N\sup_{(P_N,\mathcal S_N)\in\mathcal M}E_{P_N}[(\widetilde\beta_N-\beta)^2]\ge c\).
statements.justification: The converse certifies that the uniform profile procedure attains the honest length and risk rates even though \(p\) is unidentified at zero amplitude.
statements.gap: Li's scalar microergodic Gaussian limit and Cai--Low's abstract modulus theory do not give a lower bound for the complete bivariate observed field with the slope and cross-tail nuisance.
statements.consumer: It rules out claims that another spatial adjustment can uniformly deliver intervals of smaller order on the stated no-nugget model.

statements.statement: When \(d=1\), \(D=[0,1]\), the sites are equally spaced, and the marginal ranges coincide, the leading covariance shape is \(H_N\to\begin{pmatrix}1&1&1\\1&2&2\\1&2&4\end{pmatrix}\) and \(q_N(p)\to(1,2^{2p-1},4^{2p-1})^{\mathsf T}\). Thus the proposed experiment reduces to the known Ornstein--Uhlenbeck nested-increment Gaussian limit, while the profile construction remains nonsingular at \(A=0\).
statements.justification: This reduction is the required sanity check and fixes the covariance and mean normalizations in a fully tractable special case.
statements.gap: Known two-scale cancellation assumes \(p\) known; the three-scale profiled reduction remains regular for \(\beta\) when \(p\) is unidentified.
statements.consumer: It supplies a reproducible benchmark for implementations and for checking all constants in the general-design theorem.

statements.statement: Can the attainable Gaussian-tube calibration handle construct \(\widetilde C_N\) with \(\lim_{N\to\infty}\inf_{(P_N,\mathcal S_N)\in\mathcal M}P_N\{\beta\in\widetilde C_N\}=1-\alpha\), a uniformly continuous reference quantile, and a certified approximation from above, simultaneously for \(\lambda_N=0\), bounded local amplitudes, diverging amplitudes, exponent endpoints, and nonconvergent allowed design sequences?
statements.justification: This is the nonroutine open step separating conservative honesty from exact least-favorable coverage with attainable critical values.
statements.gap: Andrews and Mikusheva establish generic conditional size control, but they do not analyze this curved cone, its diverging-amplitude tangent limits, or certified continuum optimization on changing spatial designs.
statements.consumer: A positive answer yields less conservative reported intervals while preserving the uniform guarantee needed for the county-centroid application.

sampling_model.design: Deterministic quasi-uniform triangular arrays in a fixed bounded Lipschitz domain in \(d\in\{1,2\}\), with \(h_N\asymp N^{-1/d}\) and separation comparable to \(h_N\).
sampling_model.units: The observed units are sites \(s_{i,N}\); uncertainty comes from one centered stationary bivariate Gaussian-field realization evaluated at those sites.
sampling_model.treatment: The continuous exposure is \(X(s_{i,N})\), and the homogeneous conditional slope in \(Y(s)=\beta X(s)+W(s)\) is the target.
sampling_model.overlap: No exposure nugget or nonspatial variation is assumed; identification comes from the smoother signed cross-tail with \(p\in[p_{\min},p_{\max}]\subset(1/2,1)\).
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Only the marginal microergodic scale ratio \(\gamma=c_W/c_X\) is estimated by residual quadratic variations; \(p\), \(A\), and the nonmicroergodic ranges are profiled or bounded over their stipulated compact sets.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: High-frequency dissipation of exposure--confounder coherence supplies sufficient identification and motivates spectral adjustment.
Relative local smoothness conditions characterize consistent slope estimability and local differences or Laplacians yield consistent estimators.
Locally preconditioned inversion-free covariance estimators are root-\(N\) consistent and asymptotically normal on multidimensional irregular lattices.
Higher-order quadratic variations consistently estimate Mat\'ern smoothness and microergodic parameters on three structured irregular-design families.
Appropriately filtered smoothed spatial cross-periodograms on lattices are relatively consistent and asymptotically normal.
The scalar Mat\'ern microergodic parameter has root-\(N\) Gaussian behavior uniformly over a compact nuisance range with known smoothness.
Conditional quasi-likelihood-ratio tests have uniformly correct asymptotic size without restrictions on identification strength.
A plurality-rule aggregate mode consistently estimates the spatial slope, and valid candidate slopes are asymptotically normal.

tldr: High-frequency separation can identify a spatial slope even without nugget variation, but existing theory does not justify confidence intervals when the signed cross-tail shrinks to zero and its exponent disappears. Three exact affine-annihilating local slopes generate a finite-dimensional mean cone \(\beta\mathbf 1+B_Nq_N(p)\) whose secants and tangents remain uniformly separated from the slope direction. The central theorem derives the corresponding Gaussian experiment and feasible scale studentization on the actual quasi-uniform design, yielding uniformly honest root-\(N\) confidence sets and root-\(N\) risk through every \(A_N\to0\); a complete-data Gaussian lower bound matches both rates. Exact attainable least-favorable calibration, beyond conservative chi-square coverage, is the explicit open question.

project_justification.gap: Published spatial-confounding results identify or consistently estimate slopes under local spectral separation, and published fixed-domain results deliver Gaussian inference for scalar covariance combinations. They do not provide design-uniform slope inference when the observation-scale cross-tail is local to zero and its exponent is unidentified.
project_justification.niche: The exact Mat\'ern-one-half, no-nugget model isolates a nonregular but finite-dimensional nuisance geometry in which three scales separate \(\beta\) uniformly, while affine filters make arbitrary quasi-uniform designs analytically tractable in dimensions one and two.
project_justification.fill: The project derives the actual-design Gaussian experiment, residual-scale studentization, conservative uniform coverage, root-\(N\) diameter and risk, and matching honest lower bounds, while exposing attainable exact calibration as a sharply delimited open theorem.

related_work: Guan, Page, Reich, Ventrucci and Yang motivate the problem by showing that decay of high-frequency exposure--confounder coherence can identify a spatial slope; their spectral construction informs the observation-scale tail parameter used here. Datta and Stein characterize consistent infill estimability and construct local-difference and Laplacian estimators over broad Gaussian-field classes; their result informs the local-filter architecture, while the present target is uniform inference on a narrower signed-cross-tail class. Keshavarz, Nguyen and Scott obtain root-\(N\) Gaussian covariance estimation from preconditioned quadratic forms on irregular lattices, and Loh, Sun and Wen develop higher-order variations on selected irregular designs; both inform the finite-matrix proof. Lim and Stein prove normality of filtered cross-periodograms on lattices and inform the cross-form covariance analysis. Zhang and Li establish the scalar Mat\'ern microergodic geometry and root-\(N\) inference over range nuisance, respectively. Andrews and Mikusheva inform calibration under weak identification but do not supply the spatial experiment. Burman, Ogburn and Datta provide the conditional PM2.5 and COVID-19 consumer and a distinct plurality-based identifying model.
technical_internal_limitation: First differences are insufficient in \(d=2\): the analytic covariance remainder creates an \(O(h_N)\) slope bias and normalized correlations of order \(1/r\) create a logarithmic variance factor. Exact affine annihilation removes the quadratic covariance term and yields summable fourth-difference dependence. Three-scale profile intervals may nevertheless have large constants when \(p_{\min}\) is close to \(1/2\); the proposal claims rate optimality, not an efficient constant.
honest_scope: The conservative chi-square confidence theorem, root-\(N\) risk and length bounds, and rate lower bound are the principal claims to prove. Equality of the least-favorable coverage envelope and certified attainable quantiles remain open in Open-ended Question 1. The scope excludes nuggets, unknown marginal smoothness, nonstationarity, independent Fourier-coordinate approximations, and covariance classes broader than the stated signed bivariate Mat\'ern family. The PM2.5 and COVID-19 use is conditional on empirical Mat\'ern and quasi-uniform-design diagnostics and does not itself establish a nonparametric causal estimand.

The results cover stratified, randomized, and deformed-lattice designs rather than every quasi-uniform cloud.
seed_details.destination_search: The search paired data-driven spatial scale selection, Lepski methods, quadratic variation, and weak cross-tail inference. Scale selection can improve constants, but with only three fixed scales the exact nuisance curve already removes the logarithmic derivative.
seed_details.seed: Select the number and radii of affine stencils adaptively and prove an oracle inequality for profile-interval length.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Turn the fixed collection of variation orders into a multiscale selection rule while retaining simultaneous Gaussian approximation.
seed_details.red_team: This is tuning optimization after root-\(N\) feasibility, not a theorem-level identification or inference frontier.
seed_details.rebuttal: The objection holds for a first paper; scale optimization is a follow-on once uniform calibration is proved.
seed_details.drop_reason: The fixed three-scale experiment already gives the desired rate, leaving adaptive scale choice as a constants problem.

literature_map.settled: High-frequency decay of exposure--confounder coherence can identify a spatial regression slope, and recent path-measure arguments sharply characterize consistency for broad Gaussian-field classes.
literature_map.open_boundary: No cited theorem supplies uniform feasible inference when the observation-scale cross-tail amplitude passes through zero and its exponent becomes unidentified.

literature_map.settled: Higher-order local filters consistently estimate scalar Mat\'ern tail parameters on selected irregular designs, and filtered lattice cross-periodograms can be asymptotically Gaussian.
literature_map.open_boundary: The joint cross-quadratic root-\(N\) experiment, exact affine cancellation, and covariance consistency on every bounded-mesh-ratio quasi-uniform design are not covered.

literature_map.settled: Only Mat\'ern microergodic combinations concentrate under fixed-domain sampling, scalar microergodic parameters can have root-\(N\) Gaussian limits over range nuisance, and weak-identification-robust calibration and honest-length lower bounds have general templates.
literature_map.open_boundary: Those templates do not verify the actual spatial experiment, attainable local-amplitude set, or uniform quantile continuity for the profiled slope statistic.

literature_map.settled: Existing root-\(N\) or consistent procedures use nonspatial exposure variation, splitting conditions, or a fixed plurality of basis directions.
literature_map.open_boundary: They do not cover a no-nugget homogeneous slope identified only by a signed Mat\'ern cross-tail whose observation-scale amplitude may vanish.

literature_checklist.one_line: The survey organizes current spatial-confounding adjustments and does not report uniform fixed-domain inference through a vanishing cross-tail.

novelty_justification: The closest result is Datta and Stein's consistency characterization and local-differencing construction; the strict new object is a feasible, uniform finite-dimensional experiment for \(\beta\) with mean cone \(\{Bq_N(p)\}\), derived on the actual quasi-uniform design and valid when \(p\) disappears at \(A=0\). Guan et al. motivate local spectral separation but do not give fixed-domain uniform inference. Keshavarz et al., Loh et al., and Lim--Stein provide separate ingredients for local Gaussian quadratic forms, irregular variations, and filtered cross-spectra, but none proves exact affine cancellation, the divided-difference slope modulus, residual-scale studentization, and honest root-\(N\) profiling together. The matching lower bound is not advertised alone; it certifies that adaptation through the unidentified face costs no rate. Exact least-favorable quantile attainment remains the first-class open content.
